resolvedFindings.shot: Failure-path PNG export through an actual CPU Node stdout pipe
resolvedFindings.problem: The initial reviewed helper marked PNGs included:true but process.exit(1) cut off queued image data. In recorded child-process runs, a1500001-byte PNG reconstructed to945000 bytes and an8000000-byte PNG to840000 bytes; both reports remained complete.
resolvedFindings.why: The expanded cap does not provide lossless failed-run screenshot evidence if the process exits before the log pipe drains.
resolvedFindings.fix: Keep failure exit status1 while allowing stdout to drain. The actual updated helper uses process.exitCode=1. Read python -m json.tool /workspace/scratch/0b7ad82bafe7/ios55-followup-r2-exit-probe.json: expect reportDeepEqual=true,atCapDecodedBytes=8000000,atCapExact=true,overCapDataChunks=0 and metadata for8000001 bytes with included=false.
resolvedFindings.hypothesis: Confirmed CPU mechanism by isolated exact-footer execution: forced process.exit ends before queued stdout writes finish. A scratch one-line exitCode variant and then the actual edited helper preserve full bytes with exit1. Truncated byte count is scheduling-dependent; no claim that the same counts were measured in macOS/iOS CI.
resolvedFindings.introducedOrPreexisting: The forced-exit pattern preexists; increasing the cap exposes the defect for newly included large screenshots. This was a surviving flaw in the focused logging repair, not a newly introduced game defect.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Root changed only the final exit line and added a drain comment after the initial snapshot; exact updated helper b85b83ec116fe0187af82eca847c7d6ecb14db3e18498dcb96c228e43d285a2d passes the bounded CPU pipe check. Separate refutation status is recorded below.
